clue.text: Decent over, yes?

parts.note: time is up when it is over
'right' is an informal way of saying yes

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a matter is finished and acceptable, asking for confirmation.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and respectable, the same moral sense as decent.

clue.text: Soon member of the clergy will blow top

indicators.note: blowing one's top here means losing the head, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A warning that a churchman is about to lose his temper any minute now.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for shortly or in a little while, a synonym of soon.

clue.text: A large friendly bear standing up, fair game?

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for large
Winnie-the-Pooh, the amiable bear of A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A big cuddly bear on its hind legs, asking whether it is a legitimate target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' sounds like the idiom for a legitimate target, but here it means a game played at a funfair, where rings are thrown over prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground stall game of tossing rings over prizes, so it is literally a game at a fair.

clue.text: Solid bangle: it has broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters before it are put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sturdy piece of jewellery that has nonetheless snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangible can be touched and is real and substantial, which is a sense of solid.

clue.text: Hint about something like passport scare

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to intimate is to hint or suggest
a passport is a form of identification, ID

explanation.surface: A tip-off about something like a passport causes alarm at the border.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate is to frighten someone into compliance, a verb meaning to scare.

clue.text: Bet a butterfly can do it

definitions.meaning: second meaning: what wings do, flapping quickly and lightly

explanation.walkthrough: 'A flutter' is British slang for a small bet; the second half describes the motion of a butterfly's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a modest gamble and the quick light flapping of wings.

clue.text: View old shackle

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
to pinion is to bind or shackle someone's arms

explanation.surface: A glimpse of an antique fetter.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view one holds on a matter, as in 'in my view'.

clue.text: Cunning gags aren't very good

indicators.note: to gag someone is to stop their mouth, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: sly means cunning
ain't is a colloquial form of aren't

explanation.surface: A judgement that clever jokes are not much good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gags' reads as jokes in the surface, but it is the verb, meaning to stuff something into a mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly describes someone of exceptional virtue, hence very good in a moral sense.

clue.text: Weak girl as it happens on burgundy!

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name
a live broadcast goes out as it happens
burgundy is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A frail girl drinking a glass of burgundy wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgundy suggests the wine, but it is simply a colour. In a down clue 'on' places the second part beneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-livered means cowardly, lacking courage, which is a figurative sense of weak.

clue.text: Juvenile, unconscious criminal act

parts.note: a kid is a youngster
someone napping is asleep, so unconscious

explanation.surface: A young offender, perhaps acting without realising, commits a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapping, abducting a person, is a serious crime and so a criminal act.

clue.text: Excerpt from audiotape, little bit

indicators.note: an excerpt is a piece taken out of something longer, so the letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A short clip lifted from a sound recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota, the smallest Greek letter, is used to mean a tiny amount.

clue.text: Quick to hide damage, drug dealer

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: pacy means fast
harm is damage

explanation.surface: A narcotics trafficker hurries to conceal the damage done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' suggests a criminal, but it is a perfectly legal shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a chemist's shop which sells medicines, so it literally deals in drugs.

clue.text: Just a ban, or else reforms

indicators.note: reforms means makes over again, so the letters are formed into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A demand for justice: either a prohibition or a programme of changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and reasonable both describe something fair and sensible, as in a just demand.

clue.text: Cooked in hot liquid, layer containing grease

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a bed is a layer, as of rock or gravel
oil is a grease or lubricant

explanation.surface: Food simmered in water with a film of fat on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiled describes food cooked by immersion in boiling water, so cooked in hot liquid.

clue.text: Spilt leaving tram, sour condiment

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered about, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone spills something as they get off a tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilt' fits the condiment so well it seems part of the picture, but it only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt vinegar, brewed from malted barley, is an acidic seasoning sprinkled on chips, so a sour condiment.

clue.text: Scores progressed during games

indicators.note: during means within a period, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: ties are matches in a cup competition
went means moved on

explanation.surface: Points were racked up as the matches went on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like points in a game, but a score is twenty, so scores are twenties.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a group of twenty, so several scores are several twenties.

clue.text: Amount of liquid around lid of empty vessel

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a gallon is a measure of liquid

indicators.note: a lid sits on top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A volume of fluid in a container whose top has come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a jug alongside the liquid, but it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship, and vessel is a general word for a ship.

clue.text: Small bank, remote

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a bank is a moneylender

explanation.surface: A tiny bank branch in an out-of-the-way place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' wants to be the definition, since slender means thin; but it only gives a letter, and the definition is 'remote' as in a slender chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender or remote chance is a slight one, so both mean faint or unlikely.

clue.text: Top figure for gangster

parts.note: to cap is to top or surpass
one is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: The leading figure in organised crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago mobster of the Prohibition era, a famous gangster.

clue.text: Wind bringing flower into small city

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A breeze blowing a bloom into a little city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, in the English fens, is a favourite crossword city because it is so short.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: Opposition had to interrupt broadcast

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering it widely
taken as written

explanation.surface: Opposition politicians had to break into a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests television, but it is the farming sense of scattering seed. In British politics the opposition's frontbench team is called the shadow cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: The shadow ministers of the main opposition party mirror the government, so shadow stands for the opposition.

clue.text: Irritating little thing knocking over a fairy

indicators.note: knocking something over turns it end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an elf is a fairy creature

explanation.surface: A tiresome little sprite upsets a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny biting insect that makes the skin itch, a small irritant.

clue.text: Lively Greek character caught by superior

indicators.note: caught by means held in the grasp of, so one word is enclosed in the other

parts.note: topping is old British slang for excellent or first-rate
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A spirited Greek figure is captured by a person of higher rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toe-tapping music is lively and makes you want to tap your feet to the beat.

clue.text: Person initially sick — what might one take?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A patient who feels ill wonders what medicine to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a tablet of medicine that a sick person might take.

clue.text: Rock more noticeable, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it means judged by how the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: bolder means more striking, standing out more

explanation.surface: A rock that apparently stands out more than the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulder is a large rounded rock.

clue.text: Dog ending in shower, one with blackened face?

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dog that ends up under the shower, still with a dirty face.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, whose face gets covered in black coal dust underground.
